LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.FamilyOutcome: An outcome of a family on a finite index set S specifies one value from the alphabet of each coordinate i ∈ S.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyLawOf: The joint law of a family (Xᵢ) under p is the pushforward of p by the map ω ↦ (Xᵢ(ω))ᵢ.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMarginal: For a joint law q of an indexed family, its S-marginal is the law of the restricted vector (xᵢ)ᵢ∈S when x is drawn from q.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy: Let q be a probability mass function on the whole vector of coordinates, each with a finite alphabet. For a finite index set S, H(S) is the entropy in nats of the marginal of q on the coordinates in S.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf: Let the variables Xᵢ share a source with law p, and suppose each variable in the family has a finite alphabet. For a finite set S of indices, H(X[S]) is the entropy in nats of the joint law of the variables selected by S.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropy: Let q be a probability mass function on the whole vector of coordinates, each with a finite alphabet. For finite index sets A and B, the conditional entropy of the A-coordinates given the B-coordinates is H(A|B) = H(A ∪ B) − H(B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo: Let q be a probability mass function on the whole vector of coordinates, each with a finite alphabet. For finite index sets A and B, the mutual information between the two subfamilies is I(A;B) = H(A) + H(B) − H(A ∪ B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualI: Let q be a probability mass function on the whole vector of coordinates, each with a finite alphabet. For finite index sets A, B and C, the mutual information between the A- and B-coordinates given the C-coordinates is I(A;B|C) = H(A ∪ C) + H(B ∪ C) − H(A ∪ B ∪ C) − H(C).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropy: Let the variables Xᵢ take values in finite alphabets and share a source with probability mass function p. For finite index sets A and B, the conditional entropy of X[A] given X[B] is H(X[A]|X[B]) = H(X[A ∪ B]) − H(X[B]).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoO: Let the variables Xᵢ take values in finite alphabets and share a source with probability mass function p. For finite index sets A and B, I(X[A];X[B]) = H(X[A]) + H(X[B]) − H(X[A ∪ B]).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualI: Let the variables Xᵢ take values in finite alphabets and share a source with probability mass function p. For finite index sets A, B and C, I(X[A];X[B]|X[C]) = H(X[A ∪ C]) + H(X[B ∪ C]) − H(X[A ∪ B ∪ C]) − H(X[C]).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMarginal_re: If S ⊆ T, restricting the T-marginal of a family law to S yields the S-marginal of the original law.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMarginal_fa: The S-marginal of the family law of (Xᵢ) equals the law obtained by sampling ω from p and keeping the tuple (Xᵢ(ω))ᵢ∈S.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_eq_: For a random vector drawn from q, the entropy H(S) of its S-marginal equals the entropy of the random variable restricting the vector to S.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_e: The entropy of a subfamily X[S] under p equals the entropy of the single tuple-valued variable ω ↦ (Xᵢ(ω))ᵢ∈S.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_c: If Xᵢ(ω) = Yᵢ(ω) for every source outcome ω and every i ∈ S, the two S-subfamilies have the same entropy under p.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_emp: For a joint law on a family of finite alphabets, the subfamily indexed by the empty set has entropy zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_e: Let (Xᵢ) be a family of variables, each with a finite alphabet, on a source with probability mass function p. The tuple indexed by the empty set has entropy zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_sin: The entropy of the singleton coordinate set {i} under q is the entropy of the i-th coordinate of a vector drawn from q.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_s: Under p, the entropy of the singleton subfamily indexed by {i} equals H(Xᵢ).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_non: The entropy of any finite coordinate set in a family with finite coordinate alphabets is nonnegative.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_n: For any finite set S, the joint entropy of the variables Xᵢ indexed by S is nonnegative.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_uni: Under a joint law q, H(A ∪ B) equals the joint entropy of the two tuples obtained by restricting a random vector to A and B, including when the sets overlap.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_u: Under p, H(X[A ∪ B]) equals the joint entropy of the two random tuples X[A] and X[B], including when A and B overlap.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_tri: Under a joint law q, H(A ∪ B ∪ C) equals the entropy of the triple of subvectors on A, B and C. Overlap among the sets is allowed.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_t: Under p, H(X[A ∪ B ∪ C]) equals the entropy of the triple (X[A],X[B],X[C]). Overlap among the sets is allowed.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropy: Under a joint vector law q, the set-based quantity H(A|B) equals the ordinary conditional entropy of the A-subvector given the B-subvector.
For variables (Xᵢ) under p, the conditional entropy of the subfamilies on A given B equals the ordinary conditional entropy of the tuple X[A] given the tuple X[B].
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_: Under a joint vector law q, the set-based quantity I(A;B) equals the ordinary mutual information of the A- and B-subvectors.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoO: For variables (Xᵢ) under p, the mutual information of the subfamilies on A and B equals the ordinary mutual information of the two tuple-valued variables X[A] and X[B].
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualI: Under a joint vector law q, the set-based I(A;B|C) equals the ordinary conditional mutual information of the A- and B-subvectors given the C-subvector.
For variables (Xᵢ) under p, the conditional mutual information of subfamilies on A and B given C equals that of the tuple-valued variables X[A] and X[B] given X[C].
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropy: Under q, the conditional entropy of the singleton set {i} given {j} equals the conditional entropy of coordinate i given coordinate j.
Under p, the conditional entropy of the singleton subfamily {i} given {j} equals H(Xᵢ|Xⱼ).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_: Under q, the mutual information between singleton coordinate sets {i} and {j} equals the ordinary mutual information between coordinates i and j.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoO: Under p, the mutual information between singleton subfamilies {i} and {j} equals I(Xᵢ;Xⱼ).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualI: Under q, the conditional mutual information of {i} and {j} given {k} equals that of coordinate i and coordinate j given coordinate k.
Under p, the conditional mutual information of singleton subfamilies {i} and {j} given {k} equals I(Xᵢ;Xⱼ|Xₖ).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_: For a joint law q on a family of finite alphabets and finite index sets A and B, mutual information is symmetric, so I(B;A) = I(A;B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoO: For subfamilies of variables on a common source, I(X[B];X[A]) = I(X[A];X[B]).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualI: Interchanging the first two coordinate sets preserves conditional mutual information: I(B;A|C) = I(A;B|C).
Under p, conditional mutual information of subfamilies satisfies I(X[B];X[A]|X[C]) = I(X[A];X[B]|X[C]).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondEntropy: Conditioning on the empty coordinate set leaves the entropy unchanged: H(A|∅) = H(A).
For a joint law on a family of finite alphabets and any finite index set B, the empty tuple has zero conditional entropy given the B-coordinates, so H(∅|B) = 0.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_: For a joint law on a family of finite alphabets and any finite index set A, the A-coordinates and the empty tuple have mutual information zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualI: For a joint law on a family of finite alphabets and finite index sets A and C, the mutual information between the A-coordinates and the empty tuple, conditional on the C-coordinates, is zero.
Conditioning on the empty coordinate set leaves mutual information unchanged: I(A;B|∅) = I(A;B).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_: The mutual information of a subfamily with itself equals its entropy: I(A;A) = H(A).

Let the full coordinate vector have joint PMF q and each coordinate have a finite alphabet. For finite index sets A and B, I(A;B) = H(A) − H(A|B). The conditional entropy H(A|B) averages the remaining uncertainty about the A-coordinates over the possible values of the B-coordinates.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoO: Let the finite-valued variables Xᵢ share a source PMF, and let A and B be finite index sets. Then I(X[A];X[B]) = H(X[A]) − H(X[A]|X[B]). The conditional entropy averages the remaining uncertainty about X[A] over the possible values of X[B].
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualI: Suppose every coordinate of a jointly distributed family has a finite alphabet. For finite index sets A, B and C, I(A;B|C) = H(A|C) − H(A|B ∪ C).

Let each variable Xᵢ on a common source have a finite alphabet. For finite index sets A, B and C, the information X[B] supplies about X[A] given X[C] is I(X[A];X[B]|X[C]) = H(X[A]|X[C]) − H(X[A]|X[B ∪ C]).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_uni: The entropy chain rule with B first is H(A ∪ B) = H(B) + H(A|B), even for overlapping coordinate sets.
The entropy chain rule with A first is H(A ∪ B) = H(A) + H(B|A), even for overlapping coordinate sets.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_u: Under p, H(X[A ∪ B]) = H(X[B]) + H(X[A]|X[B]) for any two finite subfamilies.
Under p, H(X[A ∪ B]) = H(X[A]) + H(X[B]|X[A]) for any two finite subfamilies.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_: The contribution of B after A in information about C is given by I(A ∪ B;C) = I(A;C) + I(B;C|A).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoO: For subfamilies under p, I(X[A ∪ B];X[C]) = I(X[A];X[C]) + I(X[B];X[C]|X[A]).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualI: Given D, adjoining the B-coordinates to A obeys the chain rule I(A ∪ B;C|D) = I(A;C|D) + I(B;C|A ∪ D).
For subfamilies under p, I(X[A ∪ B];X[C]|X[D]) = I(X[A];X[C]|X[D]) + I(X[B];X[C]|X[A ∪ D]).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyChai: For an ordered list of coordinate indices, the entropy chain sum adds each coordinate's conditional entropy given the set of all preceding coordinates.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoC: For an ordered list of indices and a coordinate set B, the information chain sum adds the mutual information of each coordinate with B given the set of all preceding coordinates.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_eq_: For any list of indices, the entropy of the coordinate set it enumerates equals the sum of each coordinate's entropy conditioned on all earlier coordinates in the list. Repetitions are allowed.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_e: For any ordered list of indices, the joint entropy of the corresponding subfamily is the sum, over the list positions, of the entropy of that position’s variable conditional on all previous variables. Repeated indices are allowed and contribute zero on subsequent occurrences.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropy_cha: For a list of distinct indices, the entropy of the listed subfamily equals the sum of H(i|earlier indices) over indices i in order.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyEntropyOf_c: Let each Xᵢ have a finite alphabet. For a list of distinct indices i₁,…,iₖ, the joint entropy of (Xᵢ₁,…,Xᵢₖ) is the sum over positions j of H(Xᵢⱼ | Xᵢ₁,…,Xᵢⱼ₋₁). For a nonempty list the first term is H(Xᵢ₁). For the empty list the sum is zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_: For any list of indices, its subfamily's mutual information with B equals the sum of I(i;B|earlier indices) in list order. Repetitions are allowed.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoO: Under p, the mutual information of the listed X-coordinates with X[B] equals their chain sum under the family law: add I(Xᵢ;X[B]|earlier coordinates) for each list entry i, including repeated entries.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfo_: For a list of distinct indices, the mutual information between its subfamily and B equals the sum of the mutual informations between each coordinate and B given all earlier coordinates.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyMutualInfoO: For a list of distinct indices and a finite coordinate set B, the mutual information between the listed variables and X[B] is the sum over list positions of the current variable’s mutual information with X[B] given all earlier listed variables. The list and B may overlap.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.familyCondMutualI: Let q be a joint law on a family of finite alphabets, let B and C be finite index sets, and choose an ordered list of indices. The conditional mutual information between the listed subfamily and B given C is the sum of I(i;B|C ∪ E) over the positions in the list, where i is the index at that position and E is the set of earlier indices. Indices may repeat and the subfamilies may overlap.

For variables on a common source, the conditional mutual information between a listed subfamily and X[B] given X[C] equals the sum of I(Xᵢ;X[B]|X[C], earlier X-coordinates) over the list. Repetitions are allowed.
